A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial revision, both PDFs describe the same PCA-based OOD detection and RAG evaluation study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original OOD classification experiments, Neural Collapse experiments, human and LLM response evaluations, and extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and response-evaluation results and adds evaluated OOD baselines and latency measurements.

M1.justification: V2 removes the entire Neural Collapse method: clustering-based pseudo-labeling, BERT fine-tuning with combined losses, and feature-based inference scoring. The PCA projections, EVR/p-value selection, geometric detectors, lightweight classifiers, and RAG procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate COVID-19, Substance Use, StackExchange, and MSMARCO across the same 16 domains, including LLM-generated attacks and real 4chan queries. Appendix experiments retain the same data and task coverage; the new baselines and timing measurements introduce no distinct coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 1 and 7 add evaluated Mahalanobis, kNN, ViM, and ODIN comparisons across retained domains and attack settings. V1 only cited ViM without evaluating it. The NC attack-comparison column disappears, while GPT-4o prompting comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a detector-latency evaluation averaged over 300 samples with query embeddings already available, plus settings for the new baselines, including 768-dimensional representations and kNN with k=3. Existing 90:10 classification splits, response-evaluation sample sizes, retrieval settings, and annotation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 3's NC feature-separation analysis is removed, along with some attack-specific non-empty-neighborhood diagnostics from Table 2. The extensive PCA sensitivity, alternative-encoder/generator, annotation, and prompt analyses remain. V2 Table 5 summarizes an existing appendix PC interpretation analysis rather than adding a new one.

E5.justification: Both retain the same ID/OOD t-tests, means and standard deviations, agreement calculations, and five-pass GPT-4o uncertainty-aware voting experiment at temperature 0.7. V2 adds no new confidence intervals, significance procedures, or training-run/seed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained PCA accuracy cells and RAG evaluation results are unchanged. V2 adds extensive baseline results, including ODIN accuracy of 0.945 on MSMARCO and 0.353 on C19 4chan, plus latency results such as 17.7 microseconds for the geometric detector group versus 3.2 seconds for GPT-4o. NC attack results and some neighborhood percentages are removed; these are additions and removals, not improvements in retained methods' accuracy.

T1.justification: V2 removes the NC mathematical formulation, including clustering, separation and outlier-exposure losses, the combined objective, and inference score and threshold definitions. Section 5.4 and Table 4 add computational scaling analysis, including O(Dm+nm) for geometric detection versus O(nD) for full-dimensional kNN. The existing PCA and RAG mathematics remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion drop the novel NC adaptation and the contribution claiming simple methods often outperform NC and GPT-based classification. V2 centers the contribution on compact KB-aligned PCA gating and explicitly restricts its safety scope to answerability, retaining the claim that external OOD detection helps preserve response relevance.

C2.justification: V1 treats malicious queries as a subset of OOD queries. V2's introduction and Figure 2 explicitly separate KB answerability from harmful intent, explaining that harmful but answerable requests require separate policy controls. It also replaces NC mechanism interpretations with discussion of the new baselines, including a proposed explanation for ODIN's attack failures, while retaining the existing domain and language limitations.

D1.justification: V2 removes the NC training recipe and adds limited implementation information for the new baselines and timing evaluation, such as logistic-regression logits for ViM. It also discloses annotation IRB approval and compensation. Existing prompt templates, tuning tables, data sources, model identifiers, and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 abandons positioning around a novel textual adaptation of Wu et al.'s NC method and removes the Null-space Projections discussion and associated research strand. It adds Lee et al. (2018), Liang et al. (2017), and Sun et al. (2022) to support evaluated OOD baselines, repositioning the comparison around lightweight KB-aligned detection.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Separate Results and Discussion sections become a reorganized Analysis section covering detection, attacks, RAG evaluation, complexity, and interpretability. Sections and appendices gain explicit numbering, while most appendix prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 merges and transposes the central clean/attack tables and transposes the detailed domain table, adding baseline groups. It introduces the two-axis safety figure and latency table, removes the NC visualization, and redisplays selected appendix PC examples in the main text. Retained plots are unchanged but resized and redistributed within the revised layout.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer scope through the answerability/policy distinction and better supports the retained PCA approach with established baselines and previously absent timing measurements. These gains are tempered by removal of the NC investigation and useful attack-neighborhood diagnostics, while timing implementation details remain sparse. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
